question: Does a replication from the authors' public data reproduce the published difference-in-differences estimates of Card and Krueger (1994), including their standard errors and the regression sample, and how much of the balanced-sample estimate remains when extreme store-level employment changes are winsorized, a check for which no published winsorized or trimmed estimate was found (Ropponen's changes-in-changes reanalysis, which studies the distribution of effects, is cited alongside)?
hypotheses: H1 (replication; each target met if |replicated - published| <= 0.05; SE computation fixed at the design gate): (a) Table 3, row 3: NJ-PA difference 2.76 (SE 1.36), with the within-state changes PA -2.16 (1.25) and NJ 0.59 (0.54); (b) Table 3, row 4 (balanced sample): 2.75 (1.34), PA -2.28 (1.25), NJ 0.47 (0.48); (c) Table 4, column (i): 357 stores, New Jersey coefficient 2.33 (SE 1.19). Each part is reported as reproduced or not; the tolerance allows for rounding and for differences between data releases (the public files accompany Myth and Measurement, chapter 2, and may not be identical to the AER files).

H2 (a tail-only robustness check motivated by the extreme store-level changes Neumark and Wascher (1995) point to, from -41.5 to +34 FTE; a pass does not answer their broader critique that the survey's extra variability is spread through the whole distribution, not driven by a few outliers): on the H1(b) balanced sample, with permanently closed stores set to zero employment in wave 2 and temporarily closed stores missing, winsorize store-level changes in FTE employment at the 5th and 95th percentiles of the pooled distribution of those changes (closures included). H2 holds if the winsorized NJ-minus-PA difference keeps the same sign and at least half the magnitude of the unwinsorized difference on the same sample. Judged on point estimates, not significance (one treated and one control state; Conley and Taber 2011). Secondary, reported but not judged: the same with the six permanently closed stores excluded from winsorization; and Neumark and Wascher's own sample rule (drop closed stores, add chain and ownership controls), for which they report 2.78.
contribution: An independent, fully logged replication of a canonical difference-in-differences estimate from the authors' public data that also targets the published standard errors and the 357-store regression sample, which an earlier informal replication did not reproduce (the 357-store count itself was already matched at data prep with the authors' check.sas rule, so only the Table 4 coefficient and SE are tested blind); plus a winsorization check that puts Neumark and Wascher's measurement-error critique into practice; prior distributional reanalyses of these data (e.g. Ropponen's changes-in-changes) are reported in the paper. The crew had read the published results of other robustness checks; what the process rules out is specification search within this study.

design.summary: We rebuild per-store full-time-equivalent (FTE) employment from the authors' public file (njmin.zip, 410 stores) with the rules of their own check.sas (FTE = EMPFT + NMGRS + 0.5*EMPPT; wave-2 FTE = 0 for the six STATUS2=3 permanent closures and missing for the four temporary closures and the refusal) and re-estimate Card and Krueger (1994) Table 3 rows 3-4 as differences of state mean changes, with within-state SEs that allow for the same-store correlation between waves and a column-(iii) SE of sqrt(SE_PA^2 + SE_NJ^2), and Table 4 column (i) as an OLS regression of the change in FTE on a New Jersey dummy on check.sas's sample (change non-missing and either both wave starting wages present or permanently closed) with the conventional OLS SE that PROC REG reports. Each H1 target is met if |replicated - published| <= 0.05 (N = 357 must match exactly; that count was already observed at data prep, so only the Table 4 coefficient and SE are tested blind); H2 winsorizes the store-level change at the pooled 5th/95th percentiles (numpy linear interpolation, closures included) on the balanced sample and holds if the NJ-minus-PA difference keeps its sign and at least half the magnitude of the unwinsorized difference on the same stores, with closures-excluded winsorization and the Neumark-Wascher rule (permanent closures dropped, chain and ownership controls) reported but not judged. Because treatment varies only between two states, every SE is a cross-store sampling SE that cannot be clustered at the treatment level (deviation D1 from the track rules), so no hypothesis is judged on significance and no analysis runs until the design gate is approved and the Reviewer has passed a code review.
design.estimand: The difference between New Jersey and eastern Pennsylvania in the February-March to November-December 1992 change in mean FTE employment per store, interpreted (as in the paper) as the effect of New Jersey's April 1992 rise from $4.25 to $5.05 on employment at stores of the four chains in the sample.
design.identifying_assumption: Absent the rise, mean FTE employment at the New Jersey stores would have changed by the same amount as at the Pennsylvania stores (parallel trends across the two states), and no other state-specific shock between the waves differed between them. With two waves the assumption cannot be tested; no planned run can fail against it. placebo-hiwage (NJ stores paying >= $5.00 in wave 1 vs PA) is descriptive only: its published counterpart (row 3: -2.04 vs -2.16) is already known and stores at $5.00-5.04 are bound, so the paper will not cite it as support for parallel trends. This study reproduces the published estimates; it does not claim to establish the assumption.
design.method: VARIABLES (codebook column positions; check.sas formulas). FTE1 = EMPFT + NMGRS + 0.5*EMPPT; FTE2 = EMPFT2 + NMGRS2 + 0.5*EMPPT2; FTE is missing if any of its three components is missing (SAS missing-value arithmetic, as check.sas's EMPTOT). Closure override applied after construction, whatever the raw components say: STATUS2 = 3 (permanently closed, 6 stores) -> FTE2 = 0; STATUS2 in {2 renovation, 4 highway construction, 5 mall fire} (temporarily closed, 4 stores) -> FTE2 missing, except in report-only row 5 where it is 0; STATUS2 = 0 (refused, 1 store) -> FTE2 missing. DFTE = FTE2 - FTE1 (missing if either is missing), built in code/ck_analysis.py (stores.csv names: FTE = FTE1, FTE2). Store key: ROW_ID; SHEET is a label only. NJ = STATE (1 NJ, 0 PA). Chain dummies BK, KFC, ROYS (Wendy's omitted) and CO_OWNED as in check.sas. Wave-1 wage groups as check.sas ICODE: low WAGE_ST = 4.25, medium 4.25 < WAGE_ST < 5.00, high WAGE_ST >= 5.00. SAMPLES. T3-row3: wave-1 means over stores with FTE1 non-missing, wave-2 means over stores with FTE2 non-missing (unbalanced; 'all stores with available data on employment'). T3-row4 (balanced, sample B): FTE1 and FTE2 both non-missing (permanent closures in, with FTE2 = 0). T3-row5 (report only): B plus the temporarily closed stores with FTE2 = 0. T4: check.sas DATA C1 exactly: DFTE non-missing AND (STATUS2 = 3 OR (STATUS2 != 3 AND WAGE_ST and WAGE_ST2 both non-missing)); target N = 357. TABLE 3 ESTIMATES AND SEs (method S1, fixed). For state s and a sample with wave-1 set A1 (n1 stores), wave-2 set A2 (n2) and overlap A12 (n12): change = mean_{A2}(FTE2) - mean_{A1}(FTE1); Var(change) = s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2 - 2*c12*n12/(n1*n2), where s1^2 and s2^2 are sample variances (denominator n-1) of FTE1 on A1 and FTE2 on A2 and c12 is the sample covariance (denominator n12-1) of FTE1 and FTE2 on A12. On the balanced sample this is exactly sd(DFTE)^2/n. Column (iii): DiD = change_NJ - change_PA, SE = sqrt(SE_PA^2 + SE_NJ^2) (states as independent samples). Level rows 1-2 (report only): mean and s/sqrt(n) per state; difference SE = sqrt of the sum of squares. Effect size: DiD as a percent of the NJ wave-1 mean FTE on the same sample (the paper's '13 percent'). The T4 filter cascade (410 -> FTE1 and FTE2 present -> closed or both wages present) is computed in main-t4 and written to its metrics (t4_n_step1..2 by state). TABLE 4 COLUMN (i). OLS: DFTE_i = a + b*NJ_i + e_i on sample T4; judged SE = conventional homoskedastic OLS SE (check.sas uses PROC REG, which reports it); also reported: HC1 SE, N by state, root MSE (published 8.79), mean and SD of DFTE (published -0.237, 8.825). H2. On sample B: DFTE_i with permanent closures at -FTE1. q05, q95 = numpy.percentile(DFTE over all stores in B, both states pooled, closures included, [5, 95], method='linear'). Winsorized change W_i = min(max(DFTE_i, q05), q95). A store is counted as capped only if DFTE_i < q05 (low tail) or DFTE_i > q95 (high tail), strictly. Winsorized estimate = mean_NJ(W) - mean_PA(W); comparator U = mean_NJ(DFTE) - mean_PA(DFTE) on the same B (the replicated row-4 estimate). SEs for both by S1 (balanced form), reported only. H2 holds iff sign(W-estimate) = sign(U) and |W-estimate| >= 0.5*|U|, on unrounded point estimates. H2 secondary s1 (report only): the six permanent closures are excluded from the percentile pool and from capping and keep DFTE = -FTE1; the other stores in B are winsorized at the 5/95 percentiles of the non-closure pool. H2 secondary s2 (report only; Neumark-Wascher 1995 rule): sample B minus the STATUS2 = 3 stores (temporary closures are already out of B); OLS of DFTE on NJ, BK, KFC, ROYS, CO_OWNED; conventional and HC1 SEs; also the unadjusted within-state mean changes of DFTE (chg_nj, chg_pa) beside b_nj. Published comparator 2.78 with NJ +0.66 and PA -2.1 (NW 1995 p. 3, Table 1 panel A); NW's N and any further sample restriction are not recorded in sources/notes.md and are treated as unknown, so the samples may differ and a gap is not attributed to sample or specification. DECISION RULES (fixed now). H1 targets: H1(a) row 3 DiD 2.76 (SE 1.36), PA -2.16 (1.25), NJ 0.59 (0.54); H1(b) row 4 DiD 2.75 (1.34), PA -2.28 (1.25), NJ 0.47 (0.48); H1(c) N = 357 exactly, NJ coefficient 2.33 (SE 1.19). A target is met if |replicated (unrounded) - published| <= 0.05 (inclusive; compared after rounding the absolute difference to 6 decimals); a part is reproduced only if all its targets are met; point and SE targets are also reported separately. If the point targets of a part are met and only SE targets miss, the part is reported as 'point reproduced; SE construction not identified'. If S1 matches the published SEs, the paper says S1 reproduces them, never that S1 is Card and Krueger's method. H1(c)'s N target (357) was already observed at data prep (check.sas C1 count in prepare-data), so it is reported as a data check, not a blind test; only H1(c)'s coefficient and SE targets are untested. Rounding of reported numbers: 2 decimals, as in the paper. Software: Python with pandas, numpy, statsmodels from code/requirements.txt in the workspace .venv; no seeds are needed (all estimators are deterministic).
design.data: Source: njmin.zip from davidcard.berkeley.edu/data_sets (public.dat, 410 stores: 331 NJ, 79 PA; codebook; check.sas; read.me; survey instruments), the release for Myth and Measurement ch. 2, fetched by run fetch-data (size and sha256 pinned) and recorded in data/manifest.json; raw and derived data are not committed. Unit: store, keyed by ROW_ID (line number in public.dat, 1-410). SHEET is a label only: SHEET = 407 is two different stores (ROW_ID 42, PA KFC; ROW_ID 168, NJ Wendy's), so SHEET is never used as a key, merge field or cluster variable. Two survey waves (wave 1 15 Feb-4 Mar 1992; wave 2 5 Nov-31 Dec 1992). As run, prepare-data (code/prepare_data.py; documented in data/CODEBOOK.md) writes data/derived/stores.csv: 410 rows, the 46 codebook variables plus ROW_ID, FTE (wave 1), FTE2 (wave 2), CLOSED_PERM (STATUS2 = 3), CLOSED_TEMP (STATUS2 in {2,4,5}) and REFUSED2 (STATUS2 = 0), and data/prepare_metrics.json with availability counts (no employment statistic by state). The raw file already codes the six permanent closures with all wave-2 components 0 (FTE2 = 0) and the four temporary closures and the refusal with FTE2 missing; the analysis code still asserts these. Everything else is built in the analysis code (code/ck_analysis.py), not at data prep: DFTE = FTE2 - FTE, FTE2_R5, NJ, the chain dummies, the wage group, the sample flags (in_w1, in_w2, in_bal, in_r5, in_t4) and the T4 filter cascade. Checks already passed at data prep (counts only): 410 rows; 331/79 by state; STATUS2 counts equal the codebook; 321/78 wave-2 interviews; FTE available NJ 321/319, PA 77/77, both waves 309/75 = 384; NJ wave-1 wage groups 101/140/73; check.sas C1 subset 357. No statistic relating NJ to any employment variable is computed before the design gate. Known limits: no store address and no wave-1 interview date (NW 1995 fn 6), so the file cannot be linked to other data; the payroll data of NW and the BLS ES-202 data are not public.
analysis_plan: 0a. fetch-data (data-prep, data-ra; done): download njmin.zip, verify its sha256, unzip to data/raw/njmin, record in data/manifest.json.

0b. prepare-data (data-prep, data-ra; done): parse public.dat by codebook column positions into data/derived/stores.csv (codebook variables + ROW_ID, FTE, FTE2, CLOSED_PERM, CLOSED_TEMP, REFUSED2) and data/prepare_metrics.json (availability and status counts, check.sas C1 count = 357), documented in data/CODEBOOK.md. DFTE, sample flags and the T4 cascade are not data-prep outputs; they are built in code/ck_analysis.py.

0c. check-synthetic (data-prep, econometrician; allowed before the gate): code/test_ck.py runs every estimator in code/ck_analysis.py on a synthetic stores file generated with a fixed seed (no real outcome data) and asserts: S1 on a balanced sample equals the HC2 SE of the DFTE-on-NJ regression; the stacked store-wave regression reproduces the difference of state mean changes on an unbalanced sample; the winsorization caps exactly the stores beyond numpy.percentile(..., method='linear'); the T4 filter equals the check.sas C1 logic on hand-built cases.

0d. Code review (Reviewer, target 'code', reviews/code-r1): reads code/prepare_data.py (as run), data/CODEBOOK.md, code/ck_analysis.py, code/verdict.py, code/test_ck.py and the check-synthetic output against this design and check.sas. No analysis run starts until the design gate is approved AND the latest code review has no open critical or major finding.

1. main-t3 (analysis, econometrician; H1(a), H1(b)): Table 3 rows 1-5 with method S1. Metrics: n_w1_pa, n_w1_nj, n_w2_pa, n_w2_nj, n_both_pa, n_both_nj, mean_w1_pa, mean_w1_nj, mean_w2_pa, mean_w2_nj and their SEs, row1_diff(_se), row2_diff(_se); chg_r3_pa(_se), chg_r3_nj(_se), did_r3, did_r3_se, did_r3_pct; n_bal_pa, n_bal_nj, mean_w1_bal_nj, chg_r4_pa(_se), chg_r4_nj(_se), did_r4, did_r4_se, did_r4_pct; chg_r5_pa(_se), chg_r5_nj(_se), did_r5, did_r5_se (row 5 published 2.51 (1.35), report only).

2. main-t4 (analysis, econometrician; H1(c)): OLS of DFTE on NJ on sample T4. Metrics: T4 filter cascade by state (t4_n_fte_both_nj/pa, t4_n_nj, t4_n_pa), n, n_nj, n_pa, b_nj, se_nj (conventional), se_nj_hc1, const, root_mse, dep_mean, dep_sd.

3. se-alt (analysis, econometrician; report only): the SE methods not chosen, beside S1, so the paper can say which construction reproduces the published SEs: stacked store-wave regression FTE = a + b*NJ + c*POST + d*NJ*POST with CR1 SEs clustered on ROW_ID on the row-3 and row-4 samples (did_r3_cr1_se, did_r4_cr1_se, with d checked equal to did_r3/did_r4), and HC1/HC2 SEs of the DFTE-on-NJ regression on B (did_r4_hc1_se, did_r4_hc2_se; HC2 must equal did_r4_se), and the independent-waves SE of each row-3 within-state change, sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2) (chg_r3_pa_indep_se, chg_r3_nj_indep_se), since T3 uses it as an argument. Not used for any H1 judgment.

4. placebo-hiwage (analysis, econometrician; DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, no decision rule): change for NJ stores with WAGE_ST >= 5.00 minus the PA change, on the row-3 and row-4 rules, S1 SEs (plac_r3, plac_r3_se, plac_r4, plac_r4_se, n_nj_hi_w1, n_nj_hi_bal). Its answer is known from the published table (row 3: -2.04 vs -2.16), and stores at $5.00-5.04 are bound by the $5.05 minimum, so it is not a clean placebo; the paper reports it as a description and never cites it as support for parallel trends.

5. h2-winsor (analysis, econometrician; H2): on B, metrics n, n_nj, n_pa, n_closed_nj, n_closed_pa, q05, q95, did_u, did_u_se, did_w, did_w_se, ratio_w_u, capped_low_nj, capped_low_pa, capped_high_nj, capped_high_pa, capped_low_closed, capped_high_closed, fte1_mean_bal, fte1_mean_capped_low, fte1_mean_capped_high; output runs/h2-winsor/capped.csv listing ROW_ID, SHEET (label), state, tail, DFTE, W, FTE1, closed_perm for every capped store (for comparison with Ropponen's store-size pattern). did_u must equal main-t3 did_r4.

6. h2-closures-excl (analysis, econometrician; H2 secondary s1, report only): as run 5 with the six permanent closures excluded from the percentile pool and from capping. Metrics q05_nc, q95_nc, did_w, did_w_se, ratio_w_u, and capped counts by state and tail.

7. h2-nw-rule (analysis, econometrician; H2 secondary s2, report only): OLS of DFTE on NJ + BK + KFC + ROYS + CO_OWNED on B minus permanent closures. Metrics n, n_nj, n_pa, b_nj, se_nj, se_nj_hc1, chg_nj, chg_pa (unadjusted within-state mean changes); published comparator 2.78 (NJ +0.66, PA -2.1); NW's N unknown, so samples may differ.

8. verdict (analysis, econometrician): code/verdict.py reads the metrics of runs 1, 2 and 5 as --input and writes, for every H1 target, the published value, the absolute difference and a 0/1 met flag (h1a_point_met, h1a_se_met, h1a_met, h1b_*, h1c_n_met, h1c_point_met, h1c_se_met, h1c_met), and h2_sign_same, h2_half_kept, h2_holds. No judgment is made anywhere else.

9. Results review (Reviewer, target 'results'), then the PI's results gate; then the Writer; then the Replicator's clean rerun (crew.py rerun) from an environment built only from code/requirements.txt.

Any estimate not listed here (e.g. changes-in-changes, other trimming levels, Table 4 columns ii-v, Table 5 rows) is post hoc: it may appear only in a section labelled exploratory and never supports an H1 or H2 claim. If an H1 target fails, the crew reports the gap and explains it with the filter cascade and the data-vintage caveat; it does not change a sample rule, FTE definition or SE method to close the gap.
claims_plan: did-fte = main-t3.did_r3 (seed-required; macro DidFte); did-fte-se = main-t3.did_r3_se (seed-required; DidFteSe); did-fte-balanced = main-t3.did_r4 (seed-required; DidFteBalanced).
H1(a): did-fte-pa, did-fte-pa-se, did-fte-nj, did-fte-nj-se = main-t3.chg_r3_pa/_se, chg_r3_nj/_se; did-fte-pct = main-t3.did_r3_pct; h1a-met = verdict.h1a_met.
H1(b): did-fte-balanced-se = main-t3.did_r4_se; did-fte-balanced-pa(-se), did-fte-balanced-nj(-se) = main-t3.chg_r4_*; h1b-met = verdict.h1b_met.
H1(c): reg-n = main-t4.n; reg-nj = main-t4.b_nj; reg-nj-se = main-t4.se_nj; h1c-met = verdict.h1c_met.

H2: h2-unwinsorized = h2-winsor.did_u; h2-winsorized = h2-winsor.did_w; h2-ratio = h2-winsor.ratio_w_u; h2-q05, h2-q95; h2-capped-low-nj, h2-capped-low-pa, h2-capped-high-nj, h2-capped-high-pa, h2-capped-low-closed = h2-winsor.*; h2-holds = verdict.h2_holds.
Report-only: h2-closures-excl = h2-closures-excl.did_w; nw-rule-did = h2-nw-rule.b_nj; se-cluster-r3 = se-alt.did_r3_cr1_se; placebo-hiwage = placebo-hiwage.plac_r3; did-r5 = main-t3.did_r5.
Every result number in the paper comes from these claims through paper/numbers.tex macros; published numbers are citation claims already in claims.jsonl (c-pub-*).
deviations: D1 (track rule 'cluster standard errors at the level treatment varies'): treatment varies at the state level with one treated and one control state, so clustering at that level is impossible (two clusters). All reported SEs are cross-store sampling SEs, which ignore state-level shocks between the waves; following Conley and Taber (2011) they are reported only to compare with the published SEs, the paper will not present a t-statistic (e.g. the published 2.03) as design-based evidence, and H2 is judged on point estimates only.
D2: store-clustered SEs (se-alt) are reported but cluster at the store, not the treatment level; they address only the repeated observation of a store across waves.
threats: T1 Data vintage: the public file accompanies Myth and Measurement ch. 2 and may differ from the AER file, so an H1 miss could reflect the data, not the code. Addressed by: prepare-data's checks against the codebook counts and CK Table 1; the filter cascade in sample_counts.json; the paper reports every gap with its cascade.

T2 Wrong FTE or closure coding: addressed by taking FTE, the T4 sample and the chain dummies verbatim from the authors' check.sas, the closure override applied explicitly whatever the raw components hold, prepare-data's report of how the raw file codes closures, and the code review (0d). H1(a) and H1(b) separate the row-3 and row-4 sample rules through their within-state targets (NJ 0.59 vs 0.47).

T3 SE construction: the published method is not documented. S1 is fixed now because the published column-(iii) SEs equal sqrt(SE_PA^2 + SE_NJ^2) and the PA change SE (1.25) is below the independent-waves value (1.64); the NJ entries do not single S1 out (design-r1 F1: with equal variances inside and outside the balanced panel S1 implies about 0.48 for the row-3 NJ change, not 0.54), so H1(a)'s SE targets test a conjecture about the method. An SE-only miss is reported as 'point reproduced; SE construction not identified'; a match is reported as 'S1 reproduces the published SEs', not as CK's method. se-alt reports the alternatives (CR1 on ROW_ID, HC1/HC2, independent waves) without switching the judged method.

T4 Table 4 sample: fixed to check.sas DATA C1. Its count, N = 357, was already observed at data prep (prepare-data, a count only), so H1(c)'s N target is a data check, not a blind test; only the coefficient and SE targets are untested. main-t4 writes the filter cascade by state; no alternative rule is substituted.

T5 Measurement error in the survey (Neumark-Wascher 1995): H2 caps only the tails. NW (p. 9) say the excess variability is not driven by a few outliers, so a pass does not answer their broader critique; the paper must not say the result 'survives NW' (question-r3 F10).

T6 Closures drive the winsorization mechanically: the six permanent closures (5 NJ) have DFTE = -FTE1 and are among the most negative changes, so pooled capping can lift the NJ mean. Addressed by: capped counts by state and tail with closures counted separately, and secondary s1 (closures excluded from winsorization).

T7 Few PA stores: about 75 balanced PA stores, so a pooled 5% tail holds very few PA stores and one store can move the PA mean. Addressed by reporting capped counts per state and tail and the capped-store list.

T8 Store-size heterogeneity (Ropponen 2010, 2011: positive effects for small, negative for large stores): the wave-1 FTE of capped stores is reported (capped.csv, fte1_mean_capped_*), so readers can see whether capping removes large-store changes; H2 is set beside Ropponen's CIC average (0.90 vs DiD 2.72 on his 376-store support sample), not presented as the first distributional check.

T9 Parallel trends untestable with two waves: no planned run can contradict it. placebo-hiwage is descriptive (known published answer; $5.00-5.04 stores bound) and is never cited as support; the paper reports the wave-1 level gap (row 1) and states the assumption as maintained, not validated.
T10 Inference with one treated and one control state (Conley-Taber): see deviation D1; no hypothesis is judged on significance.

T11 Specification search: every run is listed in this analysis plan with its metric names and decision rule before any outcome is computed; anything else is labelled exploratory. The crew had read the published results of CK's and NW's checks (disclosed in the contribution).

T12 Code errors: check-synthetic tests on synthetic data, a Reviewer code review before any analysis run, did_u = did_r4 and HC2 = S1 consistency checks inside the runs, and the Replicator's clean rerun.

responses_design_r1.F1: T3 and method now say the NJ entries do not single out S1, pre-state 'point reproduced; SE construction not identified' for an SE-only miss and 'S1 reproduces the published SEs' (not CK's method) for a match; se-alt adds the independent-waves SE.
responses_design_r1.F2: ROW_ID is the store key and cluster variable everywhere (data, method, se-alt, capped.csv); SHEET is a label only, with SHEET 407 = ROW_ID 42 and 168 recorded.
responses_design_r1.F3: design.data and analysis_plan 0b now describe stores.csv and prepare_metrics.json as run; DFTE, FTE2_R5, sample flags and the T4 cascade (main-t4 metrics) are built in code/ck_analysis.py.
responses_design_r1.F4: T4, method and the contribution now say N = 357 was observed at data prep, so only H1(c)'s coefficient and SE targets are untested.
responses_design_r1.F5: placebo-hiwage is labelled descriptive with no decision rule; identifying_assumption, step 4 and T9 say the paper never cites it as support for parallel trends.
responses_design_r1.F6: notes.md records NW's 2.78 rule (closed stores excluded, chain and ownership controls; NJ +0.66, PA -2.1) but not its N, so the design says N is unknown and samples may differ; h2-nw-rule reports chg_nj and chg_pa beside b_nj.

tasks.title: The published estimates and definitions; later critiques and robustness checks (e.g. Neumark-Wascher payroll data, Card-Krueger 2000 reply)
Run fetch-data: download njmin.zip, verify sha256, unzip to data/raw/njmin, record in data/manifest.json
Run prepare-data: data/derived/stores.csv (codebook vars + ROW_ID, FTE, FTE2, CLOSED_PERM, CLOSED_TEMP, REFUSED2), data/prepare_metrics.json, data/CODEBOOK.md; no NJ-vs-PA employment statistic
